children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were weaker Thursday, taking back Tuesday's gains as activity resumed after the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.
- November canola was down by C$12.00 at C$811.70 per tonne.
- The Chicago soy complex was weaker on Wednesday when the canola market was closed and remained pointed lower on Thursday.
- Seasonal harvest pressure added to the declines as "the harvest window looks like it should be opened up for the next week or so," said commodity futures specialist Jamie Wilton of RJ O'Brien.
- Continued weakness in the Canadian dollar provided some underlying support, with the currency nearing its lowest level relative to its United States counterpart in 18 months.
- There were 90,639 contracts traded on Thursday, which compares with Tuesday when 80,273 contracts changed hands.
Spreading accounted for 52,660 of the contracts traded.
